subject: slavery

refused.reason: no seat counts, stocks, spends or moves enslaved people, freedpeople, fugitives or Black men as a quantity, labour or manpower: the census population is protected input read only by derivations, and people who reach Union lines are State written by regions from the derived term (SENSITIVE-HISTORY 3.2, refused, and rule 3; 0046; [SW 6.2])

no verb, option or initiative for either side to encourage, entice, prevent, recapture, count or spend self-emancipation: it is the people's own act, derived, never a lever (SENSITIVE-HISTORY 3.2, refused; [CS 4.3]; 0046)
no "suppress insurrection" action for any seat; servile war appears only as an attributed contemporary view (SENSITIVE-HISTORY 3.2, refused, and trap 8; [SW 6.8], [CS 3.1])

baselineEvidence.placementAuthority: docs/design/SENSITIVE-HISTORY.md section 3; accepted by 0046 and amended by 0074

windowBasis: [I] Candidate review envelope, not an incident trigger, publication date or proof of receipt. A named act still needs its own source/date. Inherited windows are byte-for-byte unchanged.

facets.recommendation: [I] Carry two independent routes: resistance/escape within Confederate-held territory and flight to Union lines in response to known policy and reach. No Union labor or men stock.
[I] Named, sourced arrivals can raise policy questions; people already on occupied plantations are not all new arrivals.

agencyReasonNotes: [I] Each reason names people’s own choices responding to conditions; protected inputs have no player writer. The ids are candidate vocabulary, not implemented terms.

triggerRules.policy: [I] Whole-word rules from triggerMatches; use the live proper-noun allowlist as well. A match requests review, never assigns a topic automatically. No gate:none approval is supplied.

topicRules: People are the subjects of escape, refusal, family reunion and education. Attribute Pierce/Colyer’s mediated testimony.
Separate publication dates from acts; no national total from local estimates.

examples.allowedOnlyAsWordingExample: People escaped slavery and reached Union lines.
examples.rejectExample: Union forces gained a labor pool.

remaining: National response coefficients and a complete account of resistance away from Union reach remain unestablished.
